# Trustpilot (2 endpoints)

## Endpoints

| Resource | Params | Credits | Description |
|----------|--------|---------|-------------|
| /business-search | `query` | 1 | Search Trustpilot businesses |
| /reviews | `domain` | 5 | Get Trustpilot reviews for a business |

### Parameter legend

- `a`, `b` — both required.
- `a` / `b` — a `oneOf` group: at least one member must be provided.
- `a`? — the spec marks nothing required, but these are the parameters the endpoint accepts;
  a bare call usually will not work. See Endpoint Details for which combination to send.
- *(none)* — takes no parameters at all.
- A method prefix (**POST**, **DELETE**, **PATCH**) marks a non-GET endpoint; unmarked rows are GET.
- Every endpoint also accepts the `Cache-Control` header (send `no-cache` to bypass the
  response cache — billed at the normal rate) and `Idempotency-Key` (a UUID that makes a
  retry safe; a replay returns the cached payload without double-billing).

## Endpoint Details

_What each endpoint returns and when to reach for it._

### /business-search — 1cr

Searches Trustpilot for businesses (companies) matching a keyword. Returns a unified AuthorList — each result is a business profile with its display name, Trustpilot domain (`username`/`id`), own website (`external_url`), Trustpilot review-page URL (`url`), and total Trustpilot review count (`posts_count`). Use the returned domain to pull that business's reviews via /v1/trustpilot/reviews. Note: search matches BUSINESSES, not products — a domain-shaped query returns no results. Sourced from DataForSEO's task-based Business Data API; the async lifecycle is handled server-side, so this is an ordinary synchronous request (first calls take ~15-45s, then serve from cache).

**Parameters**

- `query`: Business name or keyword (e.g. 'nike'). Matches companies, not products; do not pass a bare domain.
- `depth` *(optional)*: Number of business results to retrieve (default 20, multiples of 10, max 140). More results = longer task time.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/trustpilot/business-search?query=<query>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /reviews — 5cr

Returns a unified ReviewList of customer reviews for a business on Trustpilot, keyed by its domain (`entity_id` on every review). Each review carries the star rating, full text, title, verified-status, language (reviews arrive in many languages — filter client-side via `language`), reviewer profile, owner/brand `responses[]`, and publish date. Reviews are about the COMPANY (shipping, refunds, support), never a specific product — for product reviews use /v1/google_shopping/reviews or /v1/amazon/reviews. Get the domain from /v1/trustpilot/business-search. The platform exposes no deeper pagination — `depth` caps at 200 (the most recent / most relevant); a business with no Trustpilot reviews returns 404 (auto-refunded). Sourced from DataForSEO's task-based Business Data API (first calls ~15-45s, then cached).

**Parameters**

- `domain`: The business's domain on Trustpilot (e.g. 'www.nike.com' or 'booking.com'), from business-search.
- `depth` *(optional)*: Number of reviews to retrieve (default 20, multiples of 20, max 200). There is no pagination beyond 200.
- `sort` *(optional)*: Review ordering: `recency` (newest first, default) or `relevance`.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/trustpilot/reviews?domain=<domain>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```


## Choosing a Trustpilot endpoint

| Your goal | Use this | Credits |
|-----------|----------|---------|
| Find the business record | `/business-search` | 1 |
| Its reviews | `/reviews` | 5 |

A two-step: resolve with `/business-search` (1cr), then pull `/reviews` (5cr). Budget 6cr for
"what do customers say about X".

### What it's good for

Trustpilot skews toward **service and post-purchase complaints** — delivery, refunds, support
— rather than product quality. That makes it the right source for "is this company painful to
deal with" and the wrong one for "is this product good". For the latter, use the marketplace
review endpoints (`amazon/reviews`, `google_shopping/reviews`).

For a blended verdict across Trustpilot + app stores + Google Business + web sentiment,
`prism/reputation` (30cr) is one call. `prism/review-integrity` (30cr) additionally judges
whether a review profile looks manipulated.
